question: What is the primary function of a computer?
explanation: A computer is fundamentally designed to accept, store, and process raw data into usable information. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T5#GNS113_U1_T5_h1)

question: How do computers help nurses manage vital signs and patient numbers?

options.A: By following programmed steps to turn raw numbers into useful information
options.B: By making independent medical diagnoses using intuition
options.C: By storing information permanently without electricity
options.D: By turning handwritten notes into paper charts

explanation: Computers don't think like humans do! They rely on smart programming to turn raw numbers into clear, meaningful information for your shift. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T5#GNS113_U1_T5_h1)

question: What do we call computer hardware?

options.A: The invisible programs and operating instructions
options.B: The secret password protection protocols for patient files
options.C: The physical, touchable parts of the computer system
options.D: The wireless network signals inside a hospital ward

explanation: Think of hardware as anything you can physically touch, like the monitor, keyboard, or mouse at the nursing station. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T5#GNS113_U1_T5_h2)

question: What happens if a computer has physical parts (hardware) but no software?

options.A: The machine cannot do anything because it lacks instructions
options.B: The computer will automatically write its own programs
options.C: The hardware will melt from processing raw data
options.D: The machine will run slowly but still display patient charts

explanation: Hardware needs software to tell it what to do, just like a nurse needs clinical training to care for patients! [learn more](GNS113_U1_T5#GNS113_U1_T5_h2)

question: When a nurse scans a patient's medication barcode, which step of the computer cycle is happening?
explanation: Whenever you type, click, or scan something into the computer, you are giving it 'input'. Great job! [learn more](GNS113_U1_T5#GNS113_U1_T5_h3)

question: A low blood pressure warning pops up on your bedside monitor screen. Which computer cycle stage just happened?
explanation: Output is what the computer shows back to you on a screen or printer after it finishes processing the data. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T5#GNS113_U1_T5_h3)

question: What type of computer is the bedside tablet you use for clinical charting?
explanation: Tablets, laptops, and desktop PCs are all types of microcomputers (or personal computers) built for everyday tasks. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T5#GNS113_U1_T5_h4)

question: Why do large hospitals rely heavily on computer servers?

options.A: To replace human nurses during night shifts
options.B: To automatically inject medications into IV lines
options.C: To print out every single patient chart on paper
options.D: To store electronic health records and manage hospital network traffic centrally

explanation: Servers are powerful central computers that keep all hospital records safe and connect computers across different wards. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T5#GNS113_U1_T5_h4)

question: How do computers directly help keep patients safe during medication rounds?

options.A: By writing new drug prescriptions without a doctor
options.B: By using barcode scanning to check the right patient and drug
options.C: By removing the need for nurses to check ID bands
options.D: By physically swallowing pills to test them first

explanation: Barcode systems act as a safety net to catch mistakes before medication ever reaches the patient. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T5#GNS113_U1_T5_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a benefit of electronic nursing documentation?

options.A: Improving the legibility of health records
options.B: Keeping patient records instantly easy to view across departments
options.C: Making patient handwriting impossible for doctors to read
options.D: Supporting clinical decisions with automated alerts

explanation: Electronic charting actually fixes messy handwriting issues, making every note clear and easy to read for the whole healthcare team! [learn more](GNS113_U1_T5#GNS113_U1_T5_h5)
